value_stream.name: Supply Chain Network Design, Multi-Echelon Inventory Optimization & Flow Engineering

fields.Trigger: Strategy refresh; category review; network change

Controls: - CTL-639 (ensure controlled execution — Multi-Echelon Inventory Optimization & Service-Level Engineering (PA-136.2).)
- CTL-639: inventory strategy approved by Merchandising/Supply Chain/Finance
Cross-references: - links to VS-01 (merchandising), VS-02 (supply), VS-04 (DC/cross-dock), VS-09 (postponement/fabrication)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mis-positioning risk**: Inventory in the wrong echelon (slow at store, stockout at DC); mitigated by echelon-aware strategy
- **Postponement-overlook risk**: Missing postponement opportunities (e.g., central stock + configure-to-order); mitigated by category review
System Touchpoints: - Network/inventory model (W4122/W4130); merchandising (VS-01); supply planning (VS-02); MDM (VS-29)

steps.activity: Network Strategy/Merchandising define the inventory strategy per category: where to stock (DC vs store vs both), postponement (e.g., paint tinting at store links to VS-09), pooling, and make-to-stock vs make-to-order
steps.r: Network Strategy Lead / Merchandising / Supply Planning

steps.activity: Network Strategy set the inventory positioning policy (centralized vs decentralized, forward-stocking, cross-dock for fast-movers links to VS-04) aligned to network design (W4121)
Network Strategy document the strategy, align with merchandising/finance on the turn/service trade-off, and feed into MEIO (W4130) and parameter governance (W4135)

fields.Owner: Network Strategy Lead / Supply Chain Analytics (VS-28)
fields.Volume: ~7.2M parameter sets (per SKU per location); 35K SKUs × 205 locations

Automation Opportunity: - MEIO auto-refresh from demand/lead-time data; parameter auto-publication to MDM
Controls: - CTL-639 (ensure controlled execution — Multi-Echelon Inventory Optimization & Service-Level Engineering (PA-136.2).)
- CTL-639: MEIO assumptions documented; parameters governed before publishing
Cross-references: - links to VS-02 (supply/replenishment), VS-127 (S&OP/demand), VS-29 MDM-021 (parameters), VS-28 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Silo-optimization risk**: Optimizing each location independently misses echelon synergy; mitigated by true MEIO
- **Adoption risk**: Optimized parameters not adopted in execution; mitigated by MDM governance (W4135) and monitoring (W4138)
System Touchpoints: - MEIO optimization tool; BI/analytics (VS-28); demand planning (VS-127/VS-02); MDM (VS-29 MDM-021); ERP replenishment (VS-02)

steps.activity: Network Strategy/Analytics build and maintain the MEIO model: demand variability and lead-time variability per SKU per echelon, dependency between echelons (DC buffers protect stores), and the service-level target per segment (W4132)

Network Strategy/Analytics run MEIO optimization to find the least-inventory-cost deployment that meets service targets across all echelons (vs siloed per-location safety stock), and quantify working-capital/service impact
Network Strategy output optimized parameters (safety stock, ROP, EOQ, min/max) to MDM (W4135) for execution by supply planning (VS-02), and validate post-implementation (W4138)

workflows.name: Safety Stock, Reorder Point & Service-Level Optimization

Controls: - CTL-639 (ensure controlled execution — Multi-Echelon Inventory Optimization & Service-Level Engineering (PA-136.2).)
Cross-references: - links to VS-02 (replenishment), VS-29 MDM-021 (parameters), W4130 (MEIO), W4132 (segmentation)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Static-parameter risk**: Parameters not updated as variability changes; mitigated by refresh cycle (W4142)
- **Service-blind risk**: Inventory without service targeting; mitigated by service-level optimization per segment
System Touchpoints: - ERP replenishment (VS-02); MEIO (W4130); MDM (VS-29 MDM-021); analytics (VS-28); ABC/XYZ (W4132)

steps.activity: Supply Planning/Analytics compute safety stock and ROP per SKU per location using demand variability, lead-time variability (import 45–90d, local 7–21d links to profile), and the target service level per segment (W4132)
Supply Planning optimize the service-level trade-off per segment (cost of inventory vs cost of stockout/lost-sale), and set EOQ balancing order cost vs holding cost
Supply Planning publish optimized safety stock/ROP/EOQ to MDM (W4135), monitor service-level adherence and stockouts (W4138), and adjust on signal

fields.Volume: 35,000 active SKUs (A: top 20% = 80% revenue; B: 30% = 15%; C: 50% = 5%)

Automation Opportunity: - Auto-segmentation from sales/variability data; policy-recommendation engine
Controls: - CTL-639 (ensure controlled execution — Multi-Echelon Inventory Optimization & Service-Level Engineering (PA-136.2).)
- CTL-639: segmentation reviewed by Merchandising; policy per segment documented
Cross-references: - links to VS-01 (merchandising), VS-02 (replenishment), VS-28 (analytics), W4131 (service levels)
Pain Points / Risks: - **One-size-fits-all risk**: Same policy for fast/slow movers (over-invest in C, under-serve A); mitigated by differentiated policy
- **Stale-segmentation risk**: Segments not refreshed as SKUs move; mitigated by quarterly refresh

steps.activity: Merchandising/Analytics segment SKUs by value (ABC by revenue/contribution) and variability (XYZ by demand variability), producing a 3×3 matrix, refreshed quarterly

Merchandising/Supply Planning define differentiated inventory policy per segment (AX: tight control, high service, frequent review; CZ: minimal/no stock, make-to-order); set service-level targets per segment (W4131)
Merchandising/Supply Planning publish segmentation to MDM (W4135), drive policy into replenishment (VS-02), and review segment migration over time

fields.Trigger: Seasonal calendar; promotion plan; forward-buy decision
fields.Volume: Seasonal SKUs (~500) + promo items; Philippine seasonality (rainy, ber-months, summer)

Controls: - CTL-639 (ensure controlled execution — Multi-Echelon Inventory Optimization & Service-Level Engineering (PA-136.2).)
- CTL-639: forward-buy decisions with Finance sign-off; seasonal variance reviewed post-season
Cross-references: - links to VS-01/VS-101 (merch financial/seasonal), VS-106 (commodity), VS-39/VS-58 (promo), VS-64 (clearance)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-stock risk**: Seasonal over-buy → markdown/clearance; mitigated by forecast discipline and phase-out (VS-64)
- **Stockout-risk**: Under-buy during peak → lost sales; mitigated by buffer planning and pre-positioning

steps.activity: Supply Planning/Merchandising plan seasonal/promotional buffers using the seasonal calendar (links to VS-01/VS-101), forecast lift, and lead time; pre-position ahead of season (links to VS-02.3 W1432/W1492)
Supply Planning/Finance evaluate forward-buy decisions (commodity price links to VS-106, promo/MDF links to VS-39), balance inventory carry vs price advantage, and set promo stock vs regular
Supply Planning monitor seasonal sell-through and post-season clearance (links to VS-64), and capture lessons for next cycle (W4144)

fields.Participants: Merchandising (VS-01), Supply Planning (VS-02), Inventory Lifecycle (VS-05), Finance (VS-17.4)
fields.Volume: ~50% of SKUs are C-items (long tail); obsolescence exposure

Controls: - CTL-80 (ensure inventory parameter & network optimization governance.)
- CTL-639: write-downs per accounting policy (VS-17); slow-mover decisions documented
Cross-references: - links to VS-05 (inventory aging/lifecycle), VS-01 (lifecycle/assortment), VS-09 (special order), VS-17 (write-downs)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Dead-stock risk**: Capital trapped in non-moving inventory; mitigated by centralization and clearance
- **Service-risk**: Over-aggressive cut harming availability of needed items; mitigated by segment-aware policy (W4132)
System Touchpoints: - Inventory aging (VS-05); merchandising/lifecycle (VS-01); finance/write-down (VS-17); special order (VS-09)

steps.activity: Merchandising/Supply Planning identify slow-movers/long-tail (CZ segment) and obsolescence risk via aging analysis (links to VS-05 inventory aging), and quantify carrying cost and write-down exposure

Merchandising optimize slow-movers: centralize stocking (stock at DC only, store-on-request), convert to non-stock/special-order (links to VS-09), bundle/clearance (links to VS-64/VS-32), or discontinue (links to VS-01 lifecycle)
Merchandising/Finance manage obsolescence reserves/write-downs (links to VS-17), and feed slow-mover learnings into assortment (VS-01)

fields.Participants: Supply Planning (VS-02), MDM (VS-29 MDM-021), Merchandising (VS-01), Audit (VS-21)
fields.Volume: ~7.2M parameter sets (ROP, safety stock, EOQ, min/max, lead time, MOQ)

Automation Opportunity: - Parameter-change workflow with validation; drift detection
Controls: - CTL-80 (ensure inventory parameter & network optimization governance.)
- CTL-639: parameter changes approved and audited (MDM-021); exception overrides documented
Cross-references: - links to VS-29 MDM-021 (replenishment parameters), VS-45 (consignment/VMI), VS-02 (replenishment)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Rogue-parameter risk**: Manual overrides not governed; mitigated by approval and audit trail
- **Parameter-drift risk**: Parameters not refreshed; mitigated by governance and refresh cycle (W4142)
System Touchpoints: - MDM (VS-29 MDM-021); ERP replenishment (VS-02); MEIO (W4130); audit (VS-21)

steps.activity: Supply Planning/MDM govern inventory parameters (ROP, safety stock, EOQ, min/max, lead time, MOQ) per the MDM-021 standard (links to VS-29), with calculation validation, effective-dating, and approval
Supply Planning manage exception parameters (consignment links to VS-45, VMI links to VS-45, DSD links to PUR-013, non-stock) and overrides with effective dating
Supply Planning/MDM maintain parameter audit trail, reconcile parameters vs MEIO outputs (W4130/W4131), and support audit (VS-21)

fields.Trigger: Working-capital target; turn target; finance review

workflows.name: Inventory Investment, Turns & Working Capital Optimization

Controls: - CTL-639 (ensure controlled execution — Multi-Echelon Inventory Optimization & Service-Level Engineering (PA-136.2).)
- CTL-639: turn/service targets balanced and approved; working-capital reconciled by Finance
Cross-references: - links to VS-101 (merch financial), VS-105 (SCF/working capital), VS-17.4 (FP&A), VS-33 (performance)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Turn-vs-service risk**: Aggressive turn harms availability; mitigated by balanced targets and MEIO
- **Stranded-inventory risk**: Capital trapped; mitigated by working-capital optimization and slow-mover action
System Touchpoints: - Merch financial planning (VS-101); SCF/working capital (VS-105); FP&A (VS-17.4); MEIO (W4130)

steps.activity: VP Supply Chain/Finance establish the inventory-investment plan and turns/GMROI/WOS targets (6–8x turn) aligned to merchandise financial planning (VS-101) and working-capital management (VS-105)
VP Supply Chain drive working-capital release: MEIO (W4130), slow-mover reduction (W4134), lead-time reduction, and SCF/dynamic discounting (links to VS-105), balancing turn vs service
VP Supply Chain/Finance report inventory investment, turns, and working-capital to the executive/Board (VS-33/VS-36), and flag gaps
